j201.text: Last time: objects are made of materials. Glass is made from sand. Ceramic is made from clay. Three materials to go!

j301.text: Lock in first. A little sheep is hiding in this video. Can you spot it?

j401.text: First, wood. This bench is made of wood. So is your pencil.

j402.text: Wood comes from the trees in fields and forests.

j405.text: Look closer at this tree trunk.

j403.text: The trunks are cut into long, flat planks.

j406.text: See the lines in the plank? The bench has the same lines!

j404.text: Paper is made from wood too!

j501.text: Round one. The sole of this school shoe is rubber.

j502.text: Some rubber starts as white drops. Where do they come from? One, a cow. Two, a tree. Three, a rock. Show me with your fingers.

j504.text: One! White drops. That is milk!

j505.text: Two. I think it is a rubber tree.

j506.text: Two! A rock cannot drip. And nobody milks a shoe!

j601.text: Be a drop of sap! Shrink down. Quietly.

j602.text: You are a drop of white sap, inside a rubber tree.

j603.text: Someone makes a thin cut in the bark. You ooze out!

j604.text: You run down the cut, and drip into a little cup.

j605.text: At a factory, you are made into rubber.

j606.text: You are pressed into a shape. The sole of a school shoe!

j607.text: Now, you bend with every step.

j701.text: The answer is two. A tree!

j705.text: Look closer at the cut. White sap! Drop by drop, it fills the cup.

j706.text: At the factory, the sap is made into rubber.

j703.text: Rubber can come from the sap of a rubber tree. It can also be made by man using oil from the ground.

j801.text: Last one: fabric. Like this school T-shirt.

j811.text: Look closer at the T-shirt. Threads! Over, under, over, under. Woven threads make fabric.

j802.text: Fabric is a material that can come from animals or plants.

j803.text: Round two. This T-shirt is cotton. Where does cotton come from? One, an animal. Two, a plant. Show me with your fingers.

j805.text: One! Cotton is fluffy, like a sheep!

j806.text: Two! Fluffy white balls, on a plant!

j807.text: Two. Cotton grows on a cotton plant.

j808.text: The answer is two. Cotton comes from a plant. Wool comes from sheep. Silk comes from a kind of caterpillar.

j810.text: So sheep give wool, not cotton. Sorry, sheep!

j901.text: My notes! One. Wood comes from trees. Two. Glass is made from sand. Three. A school shoe is made of one material.

j902.text: Showdown! Double points. Which line has a mistake? One, two, or three? Show me with your fingers.

j905.text: Three! A sole, a top, and shiny rings!

j906.text: Count the parts! The sole: rubber. The top: fabric. The little rings: metal. The lace tips: plastic.

j909.text: Showed three fingers? Put up two more on your score hand!

j1002.text: Wood, metal, ceramic, rubber, glass, plastic and fabric are some of the materials we use to make the things we need.

c1003.text: Wood! Metal! Ceramic! / Rubber! Glass! / Plastic! Fabric!

j1101.text: Show me your score hand! Four fingers? High five!

j1102.text: Did you spot the sheep? It was in the field, beside the trees! Where does wood come from? Tell someone at home.

j1201.text: Next time, we test the materials! A rubber band. A wooden ice-cream stick. Which one can bend without breaking?

h860.text: Let's read today's key words together! Ready?
